newsitem.title: JAPAN: Rubber-seen easier this week after recent gains.
newsitem.headline: Rubber-seen easier this week after recent gains.

text.p: Japanese rubber futures are likely to be easier this week and undergo a correction after most contracts rose above resistance levels at 160 yen per kg last week, traders said on Monday.

But the possibility of light deliveries at the spot expiry next week as trade houses do not appear to hold ample rubber inventories, along with robust tyre demand ahead of the scheduled rise in the consumption tax in April, could limit the downside, they said.
"Rubber prices could mark time this week after the rapid price rises since the end of January," an analyst at a commodity broker said.

The TOCOM benchmark July contract could probe the downside below 155 yen early this week, depressed by a dearth of fresh factors, and a perception that the yen"s fall against the dollar has stalled for the near term, the traders said.
The most-active July contract on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) ended the morning session at 155.7 yen per kg, against 156.0 yen last Friday.
Similarly, the benchmark July contract on the Kobe Rubber Exchange was quoted at 155.4 yen in the morning session, against 155.7 yen last Friday.
Traders said open interest in rubber futures has declined despite the upward trend in prices since the end of January, which indicates lacklustre interest in rubber futures.
Open interest in Tokyo rubber futures amounted to 167,187 lots as of February 14, down from 173,175 lots on January 30, TOCOM said.
"A decline in open interest suggests that local investors have focused more on volatile commodity futures like precious metals and grains," one trading house trader said.
The trader said that is the reason why the rubber market has lacked energy to react to positive factors such as strong tyre demand ahead of the tax hike.
The offer price for Thai rubber to Japan was quoted at around $1.24 per kilo on a free-on-board basis on Monday, against $1.25 last Friday.
In the local physical market, benchmark Thai rubber for large-lot end users was quoted at 169.00 yen per kg on Monday, compared with 165 yen on February 10.
